text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish bank BPH SA, which despite dynamic deposit growth could suffer from a lack of a strategic investor, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA said in a report.

BPH has said it would like the treasury to sell much of its 46.7-percent stake to a strategic investor and also that it is mulling whether to join a group of PBR, Kredyt Bank, Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA and Warta.

"In the long run, the bank's development, to a significant degree, is dependent on the policy of the State Treasury, its main shareholder. To date it is not known what the (treasury) intends to do with its packet of shares," the report said.

The report, which was dated January 24 and released to the press on Monday, said BPH had an improving credit portfolio, with irregular receivables declining to 12.8 percent at the end of 1996's first half from 26.8 percent in 1994.
Shares in BPH, whose full name is Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA, traded at 200 zlotys at the time of the report and closed at 215 zlotys on Friday.
Handlowy said BPH's profit-growth rate similar to the level of inflation could be unsettling.
Handlowy expected BPH to lift net profit to 281.1 million zlotys in 1996 and 314.3 million zlotys this year from 244.2 million zlotys in 1995.
It saw BPH's price-earnings ratio falling to seven at the end of this year from 7.9 at the time of the report, and its price to book value falling to two from 4.2 in that period.
Preliminary figures show BPH netting 290.1 million zlotys in 1996. The bank expects to earn 333.2 million in 1997.
